title: Broadband High-Level Squeezed Light using Waveguide Optical Parametric Amplifiers with External Dispersion Compensation
authors: Takumi Suzuki, Shotaro Oki, Kazuki Hirota, Takaya Hoshi, Ryuhoh Ide, Takahiro Kashiwazaki, Taichi Yamashima, Asuka Inoue, Takeshi Umeki, Mamoru Endo, Akira Furusawa
abstract: We demonstrate broadband phase-sensitive amplification (PSA) measurement of squeezed light generated by a waveguide optical parametric amplifier (OPA) with external dispersion compensation. In broadband systems, group velocity dispersion (GVD) induces a frequency-dependent rotation of the squeezing axis, which limits the observable bandwidth in PSA measurements. To overcome this limitation, we introduce external dispersion compensation between two OPAs and suppress the quadrature rotation over a wide frequency range. As a result, we observe a maximum squeezing of 5.9 dB near the carrier frequency and more than 5 dB of squeezing up to a frequency offset of 4.5 THz from the carrier. Furthermore, squeezing below the shot-noise level is confirmed up to a frequency offset of 6 THz from the carrier, corresponding to the accessible phase-matching bandwidth of the waveguide OPA. Our results establish a practical method for broadband characterization of squeezed light and provide a key step toward ultrafast continuous-variable quantum information processing.
summary: The paper presents a method to achieve broadband characterization of squeezed vacuum states generated by waveguide OPAs. By introducing external dispersion compensation, the authors successfully mitigate frequency-dependent quadrature rotation caused by GVD. This breakthrough enables stable observation of high levels of squeezing over tens of THz bandwidths, advancing ultrafast quantum optics applications.
main_problem: The primary challenge is achieving broadband characterization of squeezed light generated by waveguide Optical Parametric Amplifiers (OPAs) while overcoming the bandwidth limitation imposed by Group Velocity Dispersion (GVD).
main_result: By implementing external dispersion compensation, the authors demonstrated maintaining more than 5 dB of squeezing up to a frequency offset of 4.5 THz, and confirming sub-shot-noise squeezing up to 6 THz.
method: The study combines theoretical modeling (Bloch–Messiah decomposition, covariance matrix formalism) with experimental measurements using two-stage OPA systems and external dispersion compensation elements.
model_or_system: The system involves a two-stage OPA setup ($	ext{OPAsqz} 	o 	ext{DC} 	o 	ext{OPAmeas}$) utilizing PPLN waveguides. The analysis tracks the evolution of quantum quadratures, incorporating effects from parametric gain and dispersion.
key_observables: Squeezing level (dB), frequency offset ($\Omega$), effective Group Delay Dispersion (GDD) ($	ext{fs}^2$), and measurement efficiency ($\eta_{	ext{eff}}$).
important_parameters: Frequency offsets up to 6 THz, optimal dispersion compensation values (e.g., $-1427 	ext{ fs}^2$), and waveguide transmittances ($T$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the state remaining Gaussian for covariance matrix tracking; in practice, continuous tuning of dispersion is difficult, necessitating pump power adjustments.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the spectral measurements showing how squeezing bandwidth broadens significantly when external dispersion compensation is applied near an optimal value. Other figures show the dependence of effective gain and efficiency on loss/transmittance.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from establishing the theoretical framework for broadband characterization, detailing the role of dispersion compensation in two-stage systems, analyzing the impact of intrinsic loss via covariance matrix methods, and concluding with experimental validation of the achieved bandwidths.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses a major technical hurdle—dispersion management—in realizing high-bandwidth quantum light sources necessary for advanced continuous-variable quantum information processing protocols.

figures.caption: Fig. 1. Conceptual model of the two-stage OPA scheme. A squeezed vacuum generated in OPAsqz propagates through a dispersion-compensation element (DC) and is measured by phase-sensitive amplification in OPAmeas. The DC element cancels the frequency- dependent quadrature rotation accumulated between the two OPAs.

Fig. 3. Simulated PSA spectra (lossless) for several dispersion-compensation values 𝐷dc: 0, −1427 (analytical optimum), −1485 (±5 THz optimum), −3384 (zero-gain limit), and −6767 fs2 (full material compensation). (a) Squeezed and (b) anti-squeezed quadratures. Proper compensation broadens the squeezed band in (a); (b) is far less sensitive to dispersion.

Fig. 4. Experimental setup. Squeezed light from OPAsqz (22 mm) is measured by PSA in OPAmeas (45 mm), both pumped at 388 THz (signal 194 THz). Fused-silica plates at the Brewster angle provide dispersion compensation. A probe beam (locked via a 99.6% mirror) and a separate lock beam (stabilized through an electro-optic modulator (EOM)) reference the two OPAs. Output is recorded with an optical spectrum analyzer (OSA).

Fig. 5. Measured spectra of squeezing (red), anti-squeezing (blue), and shot noise (black) for (a) 𝐷DC = 0, (b) 1331 (near optimum), and (c) 1997 fs2 (overcompensation), where 𝐷DC ≡|𝐷dc|. Near-optimal compensation (b) gives the broadest squeezed band.
